objective: CMFH1-CM-002. General Epidemiology and Research Methodology and Screening
stem: A 30-year-old male in a historical narrative presents to a village healer in 2000 BCE with persistent abdominal pain. The healer determines the pain is caused by the patient's 'shadow being stolen by a mountain spirit' and performs a ritualistic sacrifice. This interpretation of health and illness is best described as which of the following perspectives?

explanations.a: Biomedical perspectives rely on physiological and biological mechanisms, which were absent in ancient spiritual interpretations.
explanations.b: Evidence-based medicine relies on systemic research and clinical trials, not ritualistic or spiritual belief systems.
explanations.c: In ancient times, health was interpreted through cosmological (spirit/universe) and anthropological (human/culture) lenses.
explanations.d: While modern medicine is described as bureaucratized and politicized, ancient medicine was dominated by magic and religion.
explanations.e: Molecular and genetic perspectives are products of the 20th-century 'explosion' of knowledge.

ankiCards: In antiquity, health and illness were interpreted in a {{c1::cosmological}} and anthropological perspective.
Ancient medicine was dominated by {{c1::magical}} and religious beliefs.
Modern medicine has recently drawn from {{c1::social and behavioural}} sciences.
Medical knowledge has been derived from intuitive propositions and {{c1::cumulative experiences}}.
The goal of ancient medicine was often relief, while modern goals include {{c1::prevention}} of disease.
keyPoints: Ancient medicine was inextricably linked to religion and magic.
Cosmological perspectives link human health to the order of the universe.
Anthropological perspectives view illness through the lens of human culture and tradition.
Early medical practitioners provided relief despite a lack of scientific knowledge.
Historical medicine was built on intuitive and observational propositions.

bookReference: Man and Medicine : Towards Health for All

objective: CMFH1-CM-002. General Epidemiology and Research Methodology and Screening
stem: The evolution of medicine has progressed through various disciplinary integrations. According to the developmental timeline of medical knowledge, which of the following disciplines was the most recent to be integrated into the scope of medicine?

explanations.a: Traditional culture is the earliest source from which medicine drew its foundations.
explanations.b: Biological sciences were integrated after traditional cultures but before social sciences.
explanations.c: The text explicitly states that medicine has drawn from social and behavioural sciences 'more recently'.
explanations.d: Natural sciences were integrated alongside biological sciences in the middle stages of evolution.
explanations.e: Magical rituals represent the earliest stage of medicine in antiquity.

ankiCards: Medicine first drew from {{c1::traditional cultures}}.

keyPoints: Medicine evolves by stages, drawing from different sciences over time.
Early medicine: Traditional culture, magic, religion.

examinerTraps: Do not confuse 'Biological' with 'Recent'. While biological science is the core of USMLE-style medicine, the 'recent' expansion includes social and behavioral science.

objective: CMFH1-CM-002. General Epidemiology and Research Methodology and Screening
stem: Modern critics of global healthcare systems often point to 'social injustice' as a primary failure. In the context of 20th-century medicine, which phenomenon best exemplifies this criticism?

options.a: The lack of curative treatments for genetic disorders
options.b: The high cost and complexity of treatment preventing access at the social periphery
options.c: The failure to utilize magical and religious beliefs in modern clinics
options.d: The transition from acute care to chronic disease management
options.e: The shift of medical focus toward the Millennium Development Goals

explanations.a: While genetic disorders are difficult to treat, social injustice specifically refers to the unequal distribution of existing benefits.
explanations.b: The text states that the benefits of modern medicine have not penetrated the social periphery, leading to glaring contrasts between rich and poor.
explanations.c: The shift away from magic is considered progress, not a source of social injustice.
explanations.d: The shift to chronic care is a result of increased lifespan, not the definition of social injustice provided.
explanations.e: The MDGs are the solution to social injustice, not the example of the failure itself.

ankiCards: The 'explosion' of knowledge in the 20th century made medicine more {{c1::complex and costly}}.
The failure of medicine to reach the {{c1::social periphery}} is criticized as social injustice.
The glaring contrast in health exists between {{c1::rural and urban}} areas.
The goal of WHO is to wipe out inequalities in {{c1::health resources}}.
Modern medicine is no longer just about {{c1::treatment of sickness}}.
keyPoints: 20th-century medical knowledge made treatment complex and expensive.
Social injustice is defined by the gap between developed and developing nations.
Modern medicine's benefits often fail to reach the 'social periphery'.
WHO aims to achieve the Millennium Development Goals to address these gaps.
Healthcare is now seen as a socio-economic development tool.
microReview: Social injustice in health refers to the paradoxical situation where medicine is more advanced than ever, yet those in rural or poor areas see the fewest benefits.
examinerTraps: The trap is selecting a scientific failure (like lack of cure for cancer) instead of a distributive failure (access to care).
sourceQuote: The 'explosion' of knowledge during the 20th century has made medicine more complex, and treatment more costly, but the benefits of modern medicine have not yet penetrated the social periphery in many countries.
bookReference: Man and Medicine : Towards Health for All

objective: CMFH1-CM-002. General Epidemiology and Research Methodology and Screening
stem: Beyond the treatment of sickness, modern medicine has adopted three primary emergent goals. Which of the following correctly identifies these expanded objectives?

options.a: Eradication of spirits, purification of blood, and ritual healing
options.b: Cost reduction, privatization of services, and urban specialization
options.c: Prevention of disease, promotion of health, and improvement of quality of life
options.d: Standardization of care, bureaucratic expansion, and political lobbying
options.e: Intuitive observation, cumulative experience, and historical review

explanations.a: These are goals associated with medicine in antiquity, not modern medicine.
explanations.b: These may be economic trends, but they are not the stated 'important goals' of modern medicine.
explanations.c: The text lists 'prevention of disease, promotion of health and improvement of the quality of life' as the more important emergent goals.
explanations.d: While medicine *is* bureaucratized and politicized, these are descriptions of its current state, not its therapeutic goals.
explanations.e: These are the methods by which medical knowledge was historically derived.

ankiCards: The goal of modern medicine is no longer merely {{c1::treatment of sickness}}.
One major goal of modern medicine is the {{c1::prevention of disease}}.

Scope of medicine is regarded as an essential component of {{c1::socio-economic}} development.

objective: CMFH1-CM-002. General Epidemiology and Research Methodology and Screening
stem: A historian is analyzing the medical practices of the Middle Ages and notes that physicians of the time often consulted astrological charts before surgery. This finding supports which of the following assertions about the history of medicine?

options.a: Medical history is purely a study of discoveries and inventions
options.b: Early practitioners contributed nothing to the alleviation of suffering
options.c: Medicine is an aspect of culture and is viewed against the civilization of its time
options.d: Scientific knowledge has always been the primary driver of medical practice
options.e: Traditional cultures and biological sciences developed simultaneously

explanations.a: History is also a review of errors, false theories, and mistaken interpretations, not just discoveries.
explanations.b: The text states it would *not* be fair to say early practitioners contributed nothing.
explanations.c: The text argues medicine is an integral part of cultures and should be viewed against the philosophy and religion of the time.
explanations.d: Ancient medicine existed in an 'almost complete absence' of scientific medical knowledge.
explanations.e: Biological sciences were integrated 'later' than traditional cultures.

ankiCards: Medicine draws from {{c1::traditional cultures}} before biological sciences.
Medical history includes a review of accomplishments and {{c1::errors}}.
The relationship between medicine and human advancement is {{c1::organic}}.
Health in antiquity was viewed against {{c1::philosophy and religion}}.
Medicine in the 20th century became more {{c1::complex}}.
keyPoints: Medicine is not isolated from the cultural context of its era.
False theories (like astrology in medicine) are still part of medical history.
The study of medicine includes the evolution of human knowledge 'down the ages'.
Medical history is an aspect of the history of culture.
Historical medicine relied on cumulative experience rather than science.
microReview: Medicine is a 'mirror of culture'. In eras where astrology was part of the common worldview (cosmology), it was naturally part of the medical system.
examinerTraps: Be careful with 'nothing' or 'always'—the text explicitly says it's unfair to say early doctors contributed *nothing*.
sourceQuote: Since there is an organic relationship between medicine and human advancement, any account of medicine at a given period should be viewed against the civilization and human advancement at that time, i.e. philosophy, religion...

objective: CMFH1-CM-002. General Epidemiology and Research Methodology and Screening
stem: A researcher is studying the 'ever-changing concepts, goals and objectives of medicine.' According to the provided text, why is it essential to include 'false theories and misinformation' in a historical review of medicine?

options.a: To provide evidence that ancient medicine was the 'mother of sciences'
options.b: To justify the modern bureaucratization of medical systems
options.c: To provide a complete review of accomplishments, errors, and the evolution of human knowledge
options.d: To prove that cumulative experience is superior to biological science
options.e: To demonstrate that medical goals have remained static since antiquity

explanations.a: Dubos uses the 'mother of sciences' term to describe its cultural role, not to justify studying errors.
explanations.b: Bureaucratization is a description of the current state, not the reason for studying historical errors.
explanations.c: The text states a history of medicine contributes a review of accomplishments and errors, false theories, and misinformation to show the evolution of knowledge.
explanations.d: The text suggests science improved medicine, not that cumulative experience is superior.
explanations.e: The text explicitly says goals and objectives are 'ever-changing'.

ankiCards: History of medicine is a review of accomplishments and {{c1::errors}}.
Medical knowledge derives from {{c1::intuitive}} and observational propositions.
The evolution of medicine proceeds by {{c1::stages}} with advances and halts.

The scope of medicine has {{c1::broadened}} during recent years.
keyPoints: Medical history is not just a list of successes.
Evolution of knowledge includes 'advances and halts'.
Misinformation and mistaken interpretations are critical parts of the historical record.

objective: CMFH1-CM-002. General Epidemiology and Research Methodology and Screening
stem: Global health initiatives currently aim to attain the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs). This commitment is primarily a response to which historical trend in the 20th century?

options.a: The transition of medicine into a magical-religious framework
options.b: The organic relationship between medicine and early human advancement
options.c: The glaring inequalities in the distribution of health resources and services
options.d: The successful penetration of modern benefits into the social periphery
options.e: The reduction in the cost and complexity of modern treatment

explanations.a: This was a feature of antiquity, not the 20th century.
explanations.b: This is a general historical truth, not the specific driver for the MDGs.
explanations.c: The text states the commitment of all countries (under WHO) is to 'wipe out the inequalities' and achieve MDGs as a response to social injustice.
explanations.d: The text says benefits have *not* yet penetrated the social periphery.

ankiCards: WHO aims to wipe out {{c1::inequalities}} in health resources.
Attaining the {{c1::Millennium Development Goals}} is a global commitment.
Health contrasts between rural and urban areas are criticized as {{c1::social injustice}}.
Medicine is an essential component of {{c1::socio-economic}} development.
The benefits of modern medicine often fail to reach the {{c1::social periphery}}.

Social injustice is the contrast between health in developed vs developing nations.

objective: CMFH1-CM-002. General Epidemiology and Research Methodology and Screening
stem: The rapid advancement of scientific inquiry during the 20th century, often described as an 'explosion' of knowledge, has fundamentally altered the healthcare landscape. options.d: Standardization of health outcomes across the social periphery

explanations.a: Early medicine relied on intuitive propositions; modern scientific medicine has transitioned away from these toward evidence-based complexity.
explanations.b: The evolution of medicine has actually led to it being more heavily bureaucratized and politicized as a social system.
explanations.c: The 20th-century 'explosion' of knowledge made medicine more complex and costly, creating a gap where benefits do not reach the social periphery.
explanations.d: Instead of standardization, there are glaring contrasts and inequalities in health states between rich and poor or rural and urban areas.
explanations.e: Modern medicine has increasingly drawn from social and behavioral sciences, not reduced its influence.

ankiCards: The 20th-century 'explosion' of knowledge has made medicine more {{c1::complex}} and treatment more {{c2::costly}}.

stem: Much of medical knowledge has been accumulated over centuries through non-experimental means. From which source has the majority of early medical knowledge been derived?

explanations.a: RCTs are a modern invention of the mid-20th century.
explanations.b: The text states that medical knowledge was derived from intuitive/observational propositions and cumulative experiences.
explanations.c: Systematic reviews are the pinnacle of modern evidence-based practice, not antiquity.
explanations.d: Double-blinding is a modern scientific control measure.
explanations.e: Genomics is a product of the late 20th-century knowledge explosion.

ankiCards: Medical knowledge was derived from {{c1::intuitive}} and {{c2::observational}} propositions.
The history of medicine review includes {{c1::accomplishments}} and {{c2::errors}}.
Evolution of medicine has proceeded by stages, with {{c1::advances}} and {{c2::halts}}.
Medicine is built on the {{c1::best of the past}}.
The state of health differences between rich and poor are called {{c1::social injustice}}.
keyPoints: Medical knowledge is cumulative and experiential.
Intuition played a large role in early diagnosis and treatment.
Observational propositions led to herbal and magical practices.
Mistaken interpretations and false theories are part of medical history.
Past medical insights form the foundation of current practices.
microReview: Medical history is not just a list of successes; it is the study of human evolution and the refinement of intuitive observations into scientific knowledge over millennia.
examinerTraps: Avoid projecting modern scientific methods (like trials or meta-analysis) onto historical knowledge acquisition.
sourceQuote: Medical knowledge in fact has been derived, to a very great degree, from the intuitive and observational propositions and cumulative experiences gleaned from others.
bookReference: Man and Medicine: Towards Health for All

objective: CMFH1-CM-002. General Epidemiology and Research Methodology and Screening
stem: In a developing nation, a rural village lacks access to basic childhood immunizations while the urban capital features high-tech robotic surgery centers. This disparity in health resource distribution is explicitly criticized by international health organizations as which of the following?

explanations.a: Inequality in resource distribution is a human/social construct, not a biological necessity.
explanations.b: The text describes glaring contrasts in health states between rural/urban and rich/poor areas as 'social injustice'.
explanations.c: Cultural relativism suggests beliefs are valid within their culture, but does not address health resource inequality.
explanations.d: Natural selection is a biological concept of survival; 'social injustice' is the term used for resource disparity.
explanations.e: Economic optimization would imply this is the best use of funds, which is the opposite of the WHO's stance.

ankiCards: Contrasts in health between rich and poor are criticized as {{c1::social injustice}}.
The banner under which countries commit to wiping out inequalities is the {{c1::World Health Organization}}.
Attaining the {{c1::Millenium Development Goals}} is a global commitment.
Medicine today is heavily {{c1::bureaucratized}} and {{c2::politicized}}.
The benefits of modern medicine have not yet penetrated the {{c1::social periphery}} in many countries.
keyPoints: Global health is characterized by significant inequality.
The WHO aims to distribute health resources more fairly.
Health disparity is viewed through the lens of social justice.
Modern medicine is often too costly for the 'social periphery'.
Economic and geographic factors determine health status today.
microReview: The 20th-century 'knowledge explosion' made medicine complex and costly, leading to 'social injustice'—where advanced treatments are available only to the elite, leaving the periphery underserved.
examinerTraps: Don't confuse 'social injustice' with 'economic disparity' as the specific term used in the text for the criticism of these contrasts.
sourceQuote: The glaring contrasts in the state of health between the developed and developing countries... have attracted worldwide criticism as “social injustice”.
bookReference: Man and Medicine: Towards Health for All

objective: CMFH1-CM-002. General Epidemiology and Research Methodology and Screening
stem: The evolution of medicine is described as a non-linear process involving advances and halts. According to the historical view of medical development, what relationship exists between medicine and human advancement?

options.a: Medicine is independent of social culture
options.b: Medicine has an organic relationship with advancement
options.c: Medicine is solely a product of the 20th century
options.d: Medicine and culture are mutually exclusive
options.e: Medicine is purely a biological phenomenon

explanations.a: The text states medicine has always drawn from the cultures of which it is a part.
explanations.b: The source notes there is an 'organic relationship between medicine and human advancement.'
explanations.c: Medicine has been practiced 'from time immemorial,' long before the 20th century.
explanations.d: Medicine is an integral part of culture, according to Siegerist.
explanations.e: Medicine draws from biological, natural, social, and behavioral sciences; it is not purely biological.

ankiCards: Medicine and human advancement have an {{c1::organic}} relationship.
Evolution of medicine has drawn from {{c1::biological}}, {{c2::natural}}, and {{c3::social}} sciences.
A history of medicine review includes mistaken {{c1::interpretations}} and {{c2::false theories}}.
Medicine is built on the {{c1::best of the past}}.
The scope of medicine has {{c1::broadened}} in recent years.
keyPoints: Medicine evolves alongside human civilization.
It is a multidisciplinary field drawing from many sciences.
History includes both successes and failures (errors).
Medicine is a social system, not just a biological one.
The goals of medicine change as human knowledge expands.
microReview: Medicine is not a stagnant or isolated science; it has an organic relationship with human advancement, meaning it grows and changes as human philosophy, religion, and technology evolve.
examinerTraps: Watch out for statements that narrow medicine to 'purely biological' or 'purely scientific.' The text emphasizes its broad social and cultural integration.
sourceQuote: Since there is an organic relationship between medicine and human advancement, any account of medicine at a given period should be viewed against the civilization and human advancement at that time.
bookReference: Man and Medicine: Towards Health for All
